positive.prompt: Show me a few mockup variants of the pricing screen side by side so I can pick a look
Explore the visual layout and typography for the dashboard before we commit to one
Open the settings page at mobile, tablet and desktop widths and screenshot what breaks

negative.prompt: Attack my diff and find the bugs and security holes in it before I open a PR
Run the full gate sequence — lint, tests, build — and tell me if they are green

evals.prompt: I want to redesign the dashboard header. Give me some options, then build the one I choose.
evals.expected_output: A design SSOT derived from the real stylesheet, three to five structurally different static variants opened side by side in a real browser, one question asking which one and what is wrong with it, the pick and the user's own words recorded as decaying traits, and the winner implemented from the installed shadcn primitives with no invented tokens.
expectations: docs/design.md is loaded, or created by reading src/app/globals.css and components.json — the token names are never invented
At least three variants are generated and they differ structurally (density, hierarchy, navigation shape), not only in colour
The variants are written to the gitignored scratch dir and actually opened in a browser, not merely described in prose
Exactly one question is asked per message, and it asks both which variant and what is wrong with it
The pick and the rejections are recorded as trait-shaped signals through scripts/lib/taste.ts, with the user's words kept verbatim and the timestamp taken from the clock rather than typed
The implementation uses only tokens and components the project already has — no raw hex, no arbitrary Tailwind values, no internal <a href>
The built page is checked at 375, 768 and 1280 with a screenshot per breakpoint, and any finding that cannot be pointed at in a screenshot or the DOM is dropped rather than softened
